-(으)ㄴ 적 refers to having had the experience of doing something.
-에 = em; a repetição 손에 손 pinta as mãos: -에 marks location here. The repeated 손에 손 evokes hands joined together.
걷다 = andar; -지 é final informal de const: 걷다 means to walk. The informal ending -지 adds an affirming tone.
그런 = desse tipo; 사람들 = pessoas; 중 = entr: 그런 means that kind of; 사람들 means people; 중 means among; 하나 means one. -였어 is the informal past form of the copula.
내가 = eu como sujeito: 내가 means I as the subject of the sentence.
낯간지럽다 = dar vergonha: 낯간지럽다 means to feel awkward or embarrassed.
너 = você; 안 nega 가지다, ter; 가져 é a forma: 너 means you. 안 negates 가지다, to have. 가져 is its informal form.
a palavra inglesa para amigo, mantida na: The English word friend is kept as it appears in the lyrics.
a palavra melhor (tópico): the English word better, marked as the topic
a priori é uma expressão latina, não uma: A priori is Latin, not Korean. It refers to something understood as prior to or independent of experience. Here it works as a poetic image rather than a fully developed philosophical claim.
O BoraLang é um espaço de estudo em port: BoraLang turns your curiosity about Korean into a daily learning habit. Music draws you in; lessons help you understand, practice, and keep going. Available in Portuguese and English.
-는 건데 = terminação explicativa de cobran: -는 건데 is an explanatory ending that can sound insistent or ask for an explanation.
-ㄴ데 = terminação de confronto ou indagaç: -ㄴ데 adds background and can convey a challenge or a questioning tone.
-ㄴ데 = terminação de contexto prévio com: -ㄴ데 introduces background information with a slight contrast.
“Ê!” e “isso aí!” são aproximações do ef: English cheers such as “Yeah!” or “That’s it!” capture the energy rather than providing a single literal equivalent.
A leitura “a sensação é…” completa em po: The English wording “the feeling is…” fills out a shortened lyric fragment. There is no separately written Korean verb meaning is in this line.
님 = ser amado, pessoa respeitada (como “: 님 refers to someone beloved or respected; its precise tone depends on context. Here it is a poetic form of address.
모든 = todo; 순간 = instante. Liga-se a 잊지 못: 모든 means all; 순간 means moment. Together with 잊지 못해, the natural English reading is I cannot forget a single one of those moments.
얼음 = gelo; -들 plural; -은 tópico. Em port: 얼음 means ice; -들 marks plurality; -은 marks the topic. English usually treats ice as an uncountable noun, so it need not be plural in translation.
바다 means sea; -가 marks the subject; 들리다 means to be heard. A natural English rendering is I can hear the sea.
의미 = significado/sentido; -가 되다 = tornar: 의미 means meaning; -가 되다 means to become; -ㄴ다는 것 presents a fact as something perceived; 걸 contracts 것을. In English, takes on meaning is a natural way to express this.
좋다 = ser bom/agradável; 너와 = com você. E: 좋다 means to be good or pleasant; 너와 means with you. A natural English reading is I like the feeling of being together with you.
